newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, PGMs strongest.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, PGMs strongest.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Wednesday, with gold again seeing good volumes, but platinum group metals (PGMs) were the strongest part of the complex.

"But with U.S. interest rates heading even lower, and the stock market higher, and central bank interest in selling gold still capping the upside, the outlook is not that good," said John Maruya, chief bullion dealer for Imperial Bank in California.
"The outlook for platinum and palladium is better because of the more bullish supply side problems," he said.

COMEX August gold ended up 20 cents at $326.00 an ounce, ahead of the first notice day for the contract Thursday, but December gold is now the active contract and ended up 80 cents at $330.60 an ounce.
COMEX gold volume was again high and was estimated at 63,000 lots.

But COMEX gold open interest fell a further 4,372 lots Tuesday to 194,719 contracts, after declining from a high of 222,069 lots on July 16, suggesting much of the activity in COMEX gold recently has been fund shortcovering and rolling of positions out of the August contract.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $325.80/30, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $327.55 and the New York close Tuesday at $325.70/30.
Implied gold lease rates fell further Wednesday to around 1.63 percent for one month, from 1.83 pct Tuesday, suggesting fund borrowing to fund short positions was abating.
"Gold may possibly have begun an upside breakout on July 17, though this will have to be confirmed by subsequent events," Steven Jon Kaplan, editor of the "Gold Mining Outlook" said.
"To achieve a true upside breakout, gold must break and hold above its chart breakdown point of $326.50 (basis spot), then rally sharply in very heavy volume," he said.
Spot gold prices have edged up to near $330.00 in the past week on good volume but have encountered resistance around $330.00.
"This indicator is neutral, awaiting confirmation of the next major price move," Kaplan said.

In producer news Wednesday, another miner said its was conducting a review of its mines and development projects to determine their economics given the slide in gold prices to 12 year lows around $314.00 an ounce in early July.

Echo Bay Mines Ltd said Wednesday it would possibly defer final construction of its Paredones Amarillos gold mine in Mexico, and would review the carrying value of all its assets in view of the fall in gold prices.

Canada's Barrick Gold Corp declined comment on persistent rumors it was about to bid for Australian gold miner, Great Central Mines Ltd, to take advantage of the fall in mining asset values after the fall in gold prices.
But on a bearish note, China announced it would make no change to the present size of its gold reserves of about 400 tonnes.
In May this year, industry consultants, Goldfields Mineral Services (GFMS) said China and Russia had been buyers of gold this year, offsetting official sales from the Netherlands and Australia.
COMEX September silver ended up 4.8 cents at $4.373 an ounce, though September silver remains trapped in its $4.20-4.40 range, after spot silver saw three year lows earlier this month.
NYMEX October platinum ended up $3.30 an ounce at $424.40, after seeing a session high at $429.00, the highest levels since early June, when spot platinum saw a seven year high at $500 an ounce.
NYMEX September palladium ended up a further $3.10 an ounce at $198.00, after seeing a new life-of-contract high at $200.00 an ounce.

Russian exports of PGMs have resumed after a six months suspension, with shipments made for July under the annual supply contract to Japan, but the next deliveries are not expected to arrive until August 6 and spot market sales volumes are not meeting demand, traders said.
